title: Edo-period biographies of the Buddha and their illustrations reconfigure Gotamī (Kyōdonmi) from devoted sister to jealous adversary
authors: Namsai Tantisuk
venue: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences Studies
abstract: This study examines Edo-period biographies of the Buddha to analyze Gotamī’s (Kyōdonmi’s) roles and visual representations, focusing on how they reflect contemporary social contexts. Nine Edo-period biographies of the Buddha were included: (1) Shaka no honji (1643); (2) Shakahassōmonogatari (1666); (3) Shakahassōki tsuketari butsumomayafujin (Kateibunko version, 1669); (4) Shaka ichidaidenki kusui (1692); (5) Shaka goichidaiki eshō (1797); (6) Shaka ōkeryaku genge (1805); (7) Shaka goichidaiki zue (1845); (8) Shaka hassō yamato bunko (1845–1871); and (9) Hasshūkigen shakajitsuroku (1854). Based on analyzing these works, focusing on episodes in which Gotamī harbors malice toward Maya, this study identifies two narrative models: (1) the traditional depiction of Gotamī as the devoted younger sister who cared for Prince Siddhartha and eventually became the first bhikṣuṇī; and (2) the jealous elder sister plotting against her younger, more favored sister Maya, the Buddha’s mother, before ultimately repenting. The latter model, which emerged in the mid-17th century and persisted into the 19th, aligns with general Japanese notions of sibling hierarchy (and rivalry), wherein elder daughters traditionally held authority. Some biographies have expressed Gotamī’s envy symbolically through the imagery of a serpent, a commonly used motif in Edo society. In time, Gotamī’s visual representations have shifted from conventional “Chinese codes” to more realistic portrayals, paralleling the broader transformation of depictions of foreigners in 19th-century Japan, reflecting social change and artists’ encounters with foreigners.

title: Setting the basis for a natural language processing tool to improve the reporting of notifiable diseases: a descriptive study
authors: Clarisa Cano-Escobar; Lourdes Estefanía Barón-Miras; Juan José Gualda-Gea; Santiago Andrés Frid; M.J. Bertran
abstract: Timely reporting of notifiable diseases is crucial for public health, but it is often delayed by semimanual International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems Tenth Revision (ICD-10) coding of electronic health records (EHRs). Natural language processing (NLP) could enhance timely reporting by identifying potential cases of patients in unstructured clinical documents. This study aimed to describe the clinical documents containing key terms that suggest notifiable diseases for informing the future development of an NLP pipeline in a tertiary hospital, and this study also aimed to evaluate the current semimanual hospital notification system. This retrospective observational study included all the notifiable disease episodes according to Catalonian regulations reported between May and July 2023 from a tertiary hospital in Barcelona. Information on age, sex, notification-related variables, and the healthcare area where suspicion was determined was obtained from the hospital surveillance database. The adequacy of disease suspicion on the reporting date was assessed based on the regional public health criteria. For correct and timely notifications, the frequency of the presence of clinical documents and the frequency of their inclusion of terms that raise suspicion were described. Notification delay since the first date of evidence of suspicion in the EHR was calculated. Results were presented globally and stratified by 10 disease groups, with eight being communicable disease groups. A total of 284 episodes were notified. The most frequent group was sexually transmitted diseases (25.8%), with the outpatient clinic being the healthcare area where most notifications were found (145, 51.2%). Adequate notifications accounted for 210 (74.2%) episodes, including 25 diseases. Incorrect notifications were obtained mainly due to the reporting of chronic conditions as onset diseases (34.2%). Up to 25% of notifications were delayed for 3 days or more. Terms that raise suspicion were mostly found in medical notes (93.0%–78.7%). The unreleased clinical draft, the clinical course, and the microbiology reports were available for over 50% of the episodes of six or more disease groups, with a high inclusion of such suspicion-raising terms (81.1%–94.8%). The results revealed suboptimal reliability and faster reporting in the current reporting process. As the goal was to identify notifiable diseases before the confirmation of diagnosis, suspicion-raising terms were frequently found in unstructured clinical notes. Hence, the integration of the described documents into an NLP-based workflow could improve the reporting process.

title: Multi-sensor Calibration Technology for Intelligent Connected Vehicles
authors: Yurong Wu
abstract: Multi-sensor fusion is fundamental to environment perception in intelligent connected vehicles, but its reliability depends on maintaining a consistent spatiotemporal reference among cameras, LiDAR, millimetre-wave radar, and IMU/GNSS. This review examines multi-sensor calibration from a vehicle life-cycle perspective, focusing on how calibration parameters drift, how miscalibration is detected, when recalibration should be triggered, how parameters are recovered online, how the vehicle should operate while calibration is uncertain, and how recovery should be verified. Intrinsic, extrinsic, and temporal parameters are distinguished from pairwise and joint calibration architectures, while temporal errors are further separated into fixed offsets and time-varying synchronisation effects. Calibration methods are organised by their constraint sources, including artificial targets, natural-scene structure, and motion consistency, with learning-based approaches treated as an implementation paradigm rather than a separate information source. The review further compares requirements across end-of-line production, research platforms, and in-service maintenance, showing that in-service accuracy should be defined by downstream functional tolerance. A major remaining challenge is online verification: existing residuals and consistency checks provide only indirect evidence, while accepted criteria linking calibration uncertainty to downstream safety margins are still lacking. Future research should integrate detection, recovery, degraded operation, and verification within a unified maintenance loop.

title: Interpretation of visual sources in the museum environment: from subjective perception to algorithmic analysis
authors: Oleg Gennadievich Kovalchuk
abstract: The article presents the results of the review of the evolution of approaches to the interpretation of visual sources in the museum space, stating the transition from traditional methods based on subjective experience to algorithmic models based on artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality technologies. Based on the materials of the historical and cultural heritage of the Krasnodar Territory, the necessity of creating a comprehensive perception modeling technology that integrates blockchain verification, semantic analysis of neural networks and perceptual immersion is substantiated. An architecture is proposed that makes it possible to bridge the gap between the digital fixation of the object's shape and the transmission of its emotional and semantic content, focusing on the problem of authenticity of the digital image and the development of criteria for its comprehensive assessment. The results of the research can be applied in the creation of regional information maps of heritage and adaptive museum exhibitions.

title: Compound Fault Diagnosis for Industrial Machinery: Data-Driven Methods, Challenges, and LLM-Enhanced Perspectives
authors: Zihan Weng
abstract: Compound faults occur when several local faults exist at the same time in industrial machinery and affect condition-monitoring signals together. Their signatures become mixed through modulation, structural transmission, operating-condition variation, and sensor response, which makes feature separation and state recognition more difficult. This paper reviews data-driven compound fault diagnosis from a scenario-oriented perspective. It first summarizes the task formulation and three main difficulties: coupled fault signatures, combinatorial growth of fault states, and distribution shifts across operating conditions and machines. The review then groups representative methods into three areas: signal representation, multi-label and fault-semantic modeling, and generalization under changing domains and unseen fault combinations. The paper also examines the emerging role of large language models, focusing on retrieval-augmented knowledge integration, evidence-grounded reasoning, tool-using diagnostic agents, and deployment reliability. It then points to several directions for future work, including compositional generalization, cross-machine transfer, multimodal sensing, industrial foundation models, and autonomous maintenance. Overall, the review argues that practical compound fault diagnosis depends on combining signal-level intelligence with reusable fault semantics and verifiable knowledge-based reasoning.

title: Code Comprehensor: Hierarchical Documentation and Cross-Modal Retrieval for Large Repositories
authors: Sujoy Roychowdhury; Joseph H. R. Isaac; Jiangning Gao; Martin Klitte; Diarmuid Corcoran
abstract: Understanding large, complex, and rapidly evolving code bases remains a core challenge for software engineering at scale, hindering onboarding, maintenance, refactoring, and impact analysis. Providing this information to a Large-Language Model (LLM) is another hurdle, as the LLM must understand not only the required code method but also its associated methods in the grand scheme of the repository. We propose Code Comprehensor, a hybrid retrieval-reasoning framework combining (i) a code dependency callgraph, (ii) CodeScribe, which uses code-aware LLMs to generate hierarchical documentation across repository call graphs, and (iii) CodeContrast, a CLIP-style dual-encoder model trained on CodeScribe output to learn aligned text-code embeddings. CodeContrast enables fast, semantically precise retrieval of relevant code-context neighborhoods, which serve as grounded evidence for an MCP-based LLM orchestrator answering domain-specific queries. Evaluation on OpenCV and a proprietary 5M-LOC repository shows that CodeScribe-derived supervision significantly improves cross-modal retrieval in text-to-code accuracy over baseline approaches. Richer textual supervision (hierarchical documentation, parent/sibling context, and LLM-generated synthetic questions) consistently enhances performance across both repositories. LLM-as-a-judge evaluation using the popular RAGAS of the Code Comprehensor output yields above 90% faithfulness scores.

title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
authors: Samuel Foo Enze; Manthan Patel; Fan Yang; Linus Kramer; Pascal Roth; Marco Hutter; Cesar Cadena
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced.

title: Compositionality with Primitives: A Unified View from Euclidean to Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models
authors: Puru Vaish; Meelad Dashti; Christoph Brune; Pascal Mettes; Tatiana Tommasi; Nicola Strisciuglio
abstract: Compositional zero-shot learning (CZSL) aims to recognize novel combinations of previously observed objects and attributes. Prior work showed that large-scale vision-language models encode decomposable semantic structures that can be recomposed to enable generalization. The Geodesically Decomposable Embeddings (GDE) framework formalizes this by identifying directions in the tangent space at the Frechet mean of the embedding distribution, which encode primitive visual concepts. Unseen attribute-object compositions can be synthesized through vector addition of these primitives. We revisit the assumption that compositional generalization requires explicit attribute-object pair re-composition. By means of new compositional scoring functions and extensive evaluations, we show that directly using the decomposed primitives suffices for recognizing unseen compositions. In that, we gain insights on how the geometry of the embedding manifold (Euclidean, spherical, or hyperbolic) and dataset structure affect compositional reasoning. Across models (CLIP, DINOv2, MERU, HyCoCLIP), we show that compositional structure consistently emerges as primitive representations, enabling inference on CZSL benchmarks (MIT-States, VAW-CZSL, UT-Zappos50K, Clothing16K) and group robustness on Waterbirds and CelebA. Code: https://github.com/nis-research/Compositionality-with-Primitives.

title: Any colour you like, as long as it's UIP: Semi-simplicial types from weakenings and thinnings
authors: Thorsten Altenkirch
abstract: We explain an attempt to define semi-simplicial types (SST) in homotopy type theory by first defining a small type theory whose contexts are exactly the data of semi-simplicial types, constructing $\mathrm{SST}\,n$ uniformly in that syntax, and then interpreting the syntax in the universe. The syntax can be defined without any truncation and without K, and the construction of $\mathrm{SST}\,n$ goes through. The naive interpretation does not: it transports along the semantic images of equations that hold only propositionally, and making these transports agree needs uniqueness of identity proofs (UIP) for the semantic types. Moving the problem into the syntax, by making composition a constructor of a higher inductive-inductive type (HIIT), does not remove it either: it reappears as a coherence problem in the syntax. Fording the HIIT (storing equations instead of computed indices), with conditional rules, makes the syntax provably a set. This is UIP for the syntax, obtained by encode-decode, and it does not by itself restrict the semantics; but the naive interpretation of the conditional rules again needs UIP for the semantic types. A semantics into groupoids that avoids UIP will be discussed in a separate note. The Agda development accompanying this note is in the repository https://github.com/txa/sst-new.

title: Control-Field and Quasi-Cyclic Code Recovery in Starlink Downlink Signals
authors: Haoyan Liu; Yichuan Ma; Min Yang; Chengguang Li
abstract: Public descriptions of the Starlink downlink specify synchronization sequences, edge pilots, and predictable symbol templates, but leave the coded control fields and explicit payload-code representations largely unresolved. We examine one continuous complex-baseband capture spanning approximately 24 ms and recover control and coding structure beyond those predictable elements. Reference-phase removal exposes terminated rate-1/3 convolutional control blocks with constraint length seven and a group-level cyclic redundancy check. A conditional descriptor layout predicts sequential allocations through per-codeword symbol rounding, agreeing exactly with independently estimated endpoints in 16 of 18 frame records and within two symbols in the remaining records. Quasi-cyclic closure, binary elimination, and sparse dual checks yield explicit systematic code representations at rates 1/2 and 5/8. Frozen encoders predict 78,848, 9,984, and 811,008 reserved parity bits for three formats without disagreement. A rank-deficient long-code fit is completed within a declared finite structural family, and shared encoders are tested across modulation formats. The recovered representations explain observed coded symbols; they do not authenticate transmitter-standard identities or plaintext semantics. Two high-order formats have only one target field each, while codes 28 and 37 admit verified shortened cores with unexplained extra bits and code 4 remains unresolved.

title: YingLan: A Multimodal Ocean Foundation Model for Unified Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Observations
authors: Sen Jia; Siqi Wei; Junyu Wang; Zijun Lv; Pan Liu; Meng Xu; Xiyou Fu; Yuxi Sun; Qiang Liu; Shuyu Zhang; Lin Mu
abstract: Multimodal ocean modeling remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity in data structures, physical semantics, and spatiotemporal characteristics across satellite imagery, gridded oceanographic fields, and buoy observations. Existing approaches largely focus on task-specific ocean modeling, while learning transferable representations from heterogeneous observations remains an open problem. To address this challenge, we propose YingLan, a multimodal ocean foundation model that integrates physics-attribute-conditioned dynamic encoding, Spatiotemporal Increment Coupling (STIC), and ocean-state evolution-aware pretraining. Specifically, the dynamic encoding mechanism generates adaptive input projections conditioned on physical semantics and observation characteristics, enabling flexible representation of heterogeneous ocean variables. STIC models multiscale spatiotemporal dependencies through cross-scale interactions of latent temporal increments. The pretraining strategy further combines masked observation reconstruction with temporal evolution objectives to facilitate the learning of coherent ocean-state representations across different prediction horizons. YingLan is implemented using MindSpore and trained on Huawei Ascend 910B NPUs, demonstrating its compatibility with domestic AI computing infrastructure. In a seven-day sea surface salinity (SSS) forecasting task conducted in the Shenzhen coastal waters, YingLan achieves an average RMSE of 0.687508 PSU, corresponding to relative error reductions of 0.58%, 5.31%, and 12.42% compared with LangYa, XiHe, and GloNet2, respectively. These results provide initial evidence of the model's effectiveness in regional ocean forecasting, while broader cross-task and cross-regional evaluations remain necessary to assess its generalization capabilities.

title: CRAB: Cuboid-based Representation for As-built BIM from Point Clouds
authors: Haoran Xiong; Jing Wang; Shanshan Pan; Zihao Yan; Minglun Gong; Hui Huang
abstract: As-built BIM reconstruction from point clouds demands semantic, volumetric, parametric, and editable building components, beyond 2D layouts or planar abstractions. Yet existing scan-to-BIM pipelines often rely on handcrafted rules, heuristic optimization, or manual correction, while learning-based methods fall short of recovering wall thickness, opening geometry, and component-level BIM structure. We introduce CRAB, a BIM-ready cuboid reconstruction framework that encodes walls, doors, windows, beams, and columns as compact architectural cuboids with IFC-compatible semantics and parameters. CRAB bridges point clouds and editable BIM by combining ProposalNet, which predicts coarse component cuboids, with AssemblyNet, a relation-aware Flow Matching model that refines geometry, predicts structural relationships, and enables automatic structural correction and human-guided editing. To address limited cuboid-level supervision, we extend Structured3D with component-wise cuboid annotations and construct cuboid-based procedural scenes. Experiments show CRAB surpasses floor plan and plane-based alternatives in component completeness, geometric accuracy, and generalization. For interior wall thickness estimation, CRAB achieves a mean error of 2.80 cm, with 79.50% of matched walls within 3 cm. The project page is available at https://vcc.tech/research/2026/CRAB.

title: XingChen-UniFE: A Unified Generative Speech Front-End via Complementary Acoustic-Semantic Modeling
authors: Kelan Kuang; Qihan Hu; Jian Kang; Jie Li; Yongxiang Li; Yi Liu
abstract: This paper presents XingChen-UniFE, a unified large audio language model (LALM) for general speech restoration (GSR) and target speaker extraction (TSE). The proposed model employs complementary semantic and acoustic representations through a dual-stream encoder, where a self-supervised learning model provides hierarchical semantic features and a learnable acoustic branch captures fine-grained structures from complex spectra. A bidirectional cross-attention module further facilitates information exchange between the two representations. The fused representation conditions the LALM for discrete speech token generation with task and speaker information. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on both GSR and TSE and robust generalization to unseen degradation conditions.
arxiv_comment: Submitted to ICASSP 2027

title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
authors: Derong Yu; Guoyan Zheng
abstract: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.

title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
authors: Muhammad Ahsan Hayat; Jahangir Baig; Shayan Ahmed; Ahmed Faraz Ayubi
abstract: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: Data Representation at Scale: Extracting Meaningful Knowledge from Massive Datasets
authors: Ylenia Galluzzo
venue: Nova Science Publishers (Nova Science Publishers, Inc.)
abstract: From genomic sequence analysis to real-time sustainability monitoring, and from medical decision support to neurophysiological signal processing, Big Data meaningful knowledge extraction boosts scientific discovery and societal progress. Large-scale biological sequences reveal information about living organisms, while IoT sustainability data show how socio-environmental systems work. Clinical and imaging data support surgery planning, while EEG signals provide insights into cognitive processes. From a computational perspective, these heterogeneous sources share a common issues: transforming raw, high-dimensional, and noisy observations into structured representations that are both machine learning-ready and semantically meaningful.This PhD thesis proposes novel knowledge extraction techniques from heterogeneous and large-scale data, integrating distributed Big Data infrastructures, vector and graph-based representations, and machine learning methods ranging from classical approaches to deep learning. Heterogeneous input data, time series, images, biological sequences, and text, are processed through novel frameworks for meaningful feature extraction and embedding, producing structured latent representations Z ∈ RN×d that support statistical and predictive analysis of learned features in all domains and, in the sustainability domain, a knowledge graph that encodes relational structure between entities.Four application domains are considered: Biological data, Neurophysiological data, Sustainability data, and Medical data. For Biological data, the focus is on analyzing genomic sequences and constructing compact sequence representations that combine two complementary components: a distributed Burrows–Wheeler Transform (BWT) index, providing compressed and searchable access to large sequence collections, and the BioSet2Vec framework, devoted to the extraction of compact and statistically significant k-mer dictionaries that characterize biological sequence sets. With respect to Neurophysiological data, the aim is to extract neural signatures from EEG signals as cognitive knowledge representations. In the Sustainability context, there is modeling of stakeholder relationships via knowledge graphs and real-time energy monitoring via edge–cloud analytics. Lastly, for Medical data multimodal surgical decision support in reductive mastoplasty is addressed via probabilistic fusion of clinical and meaningful morphometric representations.

title: Formalizing the Deconstructive Narrative Model of Exclusionary Suffering: A Structural-Phenomenological Analysis of Modern Internalized Loneliness in Nikolai Gogol's The Overcoat and Anton Chekhov's Misery
authors: Yousef Madani
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This study formalizes the Deconstructive Narrative Model of Exclusionary Suffering (DNMES), a four-tiered cascading architecture for interpreting the structure and phenomenology of modern internalized loneliness in Nikolai Gogol’s “The Overcoat” (1842) and Anton Chekhov’s “Misery” (1886). While prevailing critical traditions—orthodox Marxist sociology, formalist reduction, and psychologizing biography—have treated Akaky Akakievich and Iona Potapov as objects of social diagnosis or aesthetic anomaly, the present study contends that such approaches reproduce the very epistemic exclusion the narratives dramatize. Drawing on a structural-phenomenological method and an interdisciplinary conceptual apparatus that integrates Honneth’s theory of recognition, Fricker’s account of epistemic injustice, Scarry’s analysis of pain’s unsharability, Levinasian ethics of the Other, and Derridean deconstruction, the study argues that both texts encode a social condition here termed the “apartheid of recognition”: a systemic, quasi-institutional segregation of certain subjects from the space of intersubjective acknowledgment. This segregation is enforced through an “imposed semantic blockage” that renders the sufferer’s speech inadmissible as testimony, generating at the micro-corporeal level the “Akaky Syndrome”—a somatic grammar of withdrawal—and culminating, in “Misery,” in the desperate installation of a “surrogate witness” in the figure of the horse, whose mute receptivity constitutes a paradoxical “epistemic sanctuary.” The analysis proceeds across four cascading tiers—macro-structural, meso-relational, micro-corporeal, and deconstructive-transmutational—demonstrating that exclusionary suffering in these canonical texts is not a contingent misfortune but a structurally reproducible communicative catastrophe whose logic illuminates the broader corpus of modern world literature. The study concludes that DNMES offers a transferable diagnostic framework for reading the narrative ethics of unacknowledged pain.

title: Jointly predicting courses and grades using a transformer-based model
authors: Paul Savala
abstract: Existing predictive models in learning analytics often treat student academic history as a simple sequence, overlooking the concurrent nature of courses taken within a semester. This simplification can lead to inaccurate performance predictions, particularly for students with heavy or challenging course loads. This paper introduces a TRansformer for Academic Course-grade Estimation (TRACE) that addresses this limitation by jointly predicting both the set of courses a student will take and their corresponding grades for an upcoming semester. Our approach encodes courses on a per-semester basis to capture the effects of course concurrency and utilizes a novel loss function combining course-set prediction with grade prediction. We demonstrate that predicting courses taken in addition to the grades in those courses leads to significant improvements in prediction quality. Trained on ten years of institutional data, our joint prediction model reduces mean absolute error by nearly 50% compared to an identical architecture that predicts grades alone. The model also outperforms traditional LSTM-based sequential models, as well as graph neural network-based approaches, and offers natural ways to incorporate student attribute data. This work demonstrates the utility of modern neural architectures for creating interpretable models that can be adapted to new institutions via retraining and recalibration, as well as the importance of key techniques, such as predicting courses taken during training. We discuss how this model could be incorporated into early detection systems at institutions of higher education.

title: Leveraging AI for Higher Education Human Resources:A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Maria Elena Veronica; Wendi Usino; Arief Wibowo
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource Development (HRD) policies for academic staff in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) is often constrained by the misalignment between computational capabilities and institutional governance. While HEIs generate substantial datasets through the Tri Dharma (the three pillars of higher education: teaching, research, and community service), this data remains underutilized for proactive policy-making. To map the state-of-the-art and identify existing research gaps, this study conducts a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of 400 unique peer-reviewed documents, obtained from an initial 485 records retrieved from Scopus (n = 260) and Web of Science (n = 225) after removing 85 duplicates, covering the seven-year period from 2018 to 2024. Visual analysis using VOSviewer reveals a distinct semantic-policy discrepancy, showing that semantic technologies and predictive AI models are researched as isolated technical domains, seldom integrated into comprehensive institutional governance. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a framework for Higher Education Human Resources for Lecturer Career Development. The proposed framework integrates machine learning classifiers (Naïve Bayes, K-Means, and Apriori association) with a semantic Knowledge Graph layer to transform descriptive academic metrics into explainable, policy-conforming recommendations. Preliminary expert consultation with LLDIKTI Region II highlights the conceptual viability of the Framework for Higher Education Human Resources for Lecturer Career Development in mitigating administrative bottlenecks, supporting objective career path design, and minimizing human subjectivity in lecturer performance evaluations.

title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
authors: Neel Dey; Adrian V. Dalca
abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. We use our 3D foundation model, anatomix, to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes and further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific, component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system placed first on the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at https://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.
arxiv_comment: Technical report. First place winning solution for the MICCAI Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg challenge. Code and volumetric visualizations are available at www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg . Keywords: representation learning, medical image registration

title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications
authors: Yang Luo; Tiantian Ji; Zifeng Kang; Yucheng Wang; Yong Liu; Zhiyi Yin; Xinran Liu
abstract: System One models such as Jev change how software makes decisions by mapping open-ended semantic contexts into structured judgments that directly drive program execution. However, this paradigm introduces a new security risk, which we term Jev Program Decision Hijacking (JPDH): attacker-controlled contexts can redirect program decisions through schema-valid Jev judgments. Existing evaluations focus primarily on model-level attacks or predefined injection channels, leaving attack reachability and downstream security consequences in real-world Jev applications underexplored. In this paper, we present JevProbe, the first automated framework to evaluate JPDH by tracing adversarial influence from reachable context surfaces through program-consumed decisions to downstream security consequences in real-world Jev applications. Our key insight is that application logic maps diverse Jev judgments to observable decisions, enabling systematic, program-grounded attack evaluation. Across 228 popular real-world Jev applications and 2,273 test cases, 81.5% exhibit decision flips, of which 98.6% lead to potential downstream security impacts. Compared with the strongest adapted baseline, JevProbe improves macro-average Decision Flip Rate (DFR) by 50.4 percentage points, while existing defenses offer limited protection. We further construct JevProbeBench to support systematic evaluation of JPDH in real-world Jev applications. We have responsibly disclosed our findings to Jev application maintainers, pending their responses. The source code of JevProbe and the JevProbeBench dataset are publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/xiaoxiaohg8d/JevProbe-).

title: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning
authors: Zongsheng Li; Shengyuan Zhu; Zimo Zhang; Hanyao Li; Shengming Wang; Quanying Liu
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting. To our knowledge, GeoNIRS is the first fNIRS framework to explicitly model physical channel geometry during joint pretraining across heterogeneous channel configurations, and the first to provide complete source code and downloadable pretrained checkpoints. We evaluate GeoNIRS on eight held-out tasks spanning clinical and auditory assessment, pain and affective processing, semantic decoding, and motor function. GeoNIRS achieves the highest task-averaged balanced accuracy among the evaluated conventional machine-learning, fNIRS-specific, general time-series, and fNIRS pretraining baselines. Compared with random initialization, pretraining improves average balanced accuracy by 4.12 percentage points under linear probing and 3.30 points under full fine-tuning, with larger benefits when labels are scarce. GeoNIRS also remains robust to missing input channels. Geometry perturbations and pretraining ablations further show that both channel geometry and cross-chromophore reconstruction contribute to the learned representations.

title: More Interactions Make Communications More Efficient: A Directed Information Bottleneck Approach to Task-Oriented Communication
authors: Zhirun Zheng; Yiqin Deng; Phone Lin; Yuguang Fang
abstract: Task-oriented communication improves communication efficiency by transmitting semantic information required for downstream tasks, but may incur redundancy with previously transmitted information. To address this issue, we propose a variational directed information bottleneck joint source-channel coding (VDIB-JSCC) framework that transmits only previously unacquired information. Specifically, we use directed information to characterize the causal flow of task-relevant incremental information and theoretically demonstrate its advantages over mutual information and conditional mutual information. Based on this metric, we formulate a directed information bottleneck (DIB) objective that balances task-relevant information preservation and redundant information compression. We further derive a variational formulation, termed VDIB, whose tractable upper bound serves as the training loss. The encoder integrates a Vision Transformer for frame-wise semantic extraction and a Mamba-based causal state-space model for capturing temporal dependencies and extracting incremental information, while the decoder uses a Mamba-based state-space model for task inference. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 video streams demonstrate that VDIB-JSCC achieves higher classification accuracy with less transmitted information than state-of-the-art semantic communication methods. These results show that leveraging historical knowledge enables task completion with less information, improving communication efficiency.
arxiv_comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Networking

title: LLM-based Code Auditing by Inferring and Evaluating Developer Assumptions
authors: Junming Liu; Marcel Böhme
abstract: When we see a null pointer check, we know that the developer believes that the pointer may not be initialized. If the same pointer is later used without a null pointer check, we may consider this a violation of the developer's belief and ultimately a bug. We develop such a belief-guided program analysis for vulnerability detection (VD). For example, when an authentication function returns the same error for both, a wrong user name and a wrong password, an auditor may infer that the developer believes that both cases are indistinguishable, mitigating a user enumeration attack. This belief is reasonable, as it follows standard security practice. Yet, a function call inducing a difference in response time for both cases, contradicts this belief. This contradiction uncovers a timing side-channel that syntactic analysis tools would miss. Existing static analysis tools struggle with this type of flaw because they require them to be expressible by general, syntactic patterns. Our belief-guided approach detects such domain-specific, high-level semantic security flaws that remain elusive. Given a function, our approach, Creed, infers the developer's security-related beliefs, evaluates how reasonable each one is, and derives the conditions under which it is violated. In contrast to existing ML-based VD techniques, Creed explains the root cause, the symptoms, and the conditions under which each issue is exploitable. To address the context-dependency problem in the evaluation, we introduce two measures for explanation-based VD: recall quantifies how effectively an approach correctly explains a known vulnerability, and overhead quantifies the effort of inspecting its reports. On a recent real-world vulnerability benchmark, Creed detects both semantic and syntactic vulnerabilities more effectively than existing explanation-based VD tools, achieving the best effectiveness-effort trade-off.

title: Harnessing SPAD Noise: Test-Time Gated Attention for Indoor Depth Estimation
authors: Yiquan Gao
abstract: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to hardware-dependent 3D sensing modalities, yet predicting precise metric depth remains a persistent challenge due to intrinsic scale ambiguity, edge bleeding, and limited zero-shot generalization in unseen environments. Recent multi-modal approaches incorporate 1D/3D Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) data to resolve these ambiguities, but they mainly treat SPAD noise as a harmful artifact required for denoising or leave the noise ignored. In this paper, we present an essentially different insight: native SPAD noise is an informative prior that implicitly encodes deterministic environmental characteristics. Driven by this paradigm shift, we introduce a novel, lightweight Test-Time Gated Attention framework by Harnessing SPAD Noise, therefore dubbed HSN. Tailored for indoor scenarios, HSN leverages the synergistic combination of 1D SPAD histograms and Gate Adapters (GAs). Through three complementary optimization phases, it generates channel-wise gated attention vectors to dynamically adjust encoder feature maps at inference time, effectively resolving ambiguous scale and boundary challenges without the heavy computational overhead or dense 3D modalities that other TTA methods suffer from. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world indoor benchmarks show that HSN achieves state-of-the-art metric depth accuracy in in-domain settings, while exhibiting even greater potential under zero-shot generalization to unfamiliar environments. Furthermore, interpretability analysis reveals that the proposed gated attention mechanism adaptively shifts attention toward deeper semantic layers under intensifying SPAD noise. Code will be made publicly available.

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
authors: Mohammad Abolnejadian; Matthew Brehmer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD- .txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use - - (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. Collection Size Vectors Role parliament_documents ~27 GB 768-dim, cosine Primary knowledge base retrieved during meetings vega_altair_docs ~137 MB 768-dim, cosine Vega-Altair documentation used by the visualization-generator agent Embedding model: embeddinggemma:latest (served via Ollama), 768 dimensions, cosine distance. Qdrant version: built with qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.6. Qdrant's on-disk format is version-specific, so load this snapshot with the same or a compatible version to avoid migration issues. Inspecting the knowledge base on its own To browse or query the collections independently of the InsightToast stack, mount the extracted directory into a standalone Qdrant container: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz # -> ./qdrant_storage/ docker run -p 6333:6333 \ -v "$(pwd)/qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage" \ qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.6 # reports the collection and its point count: curl http://localhost:6333/collections/parliament_documents License The parliamentary source documents and the embeddings derived from them are released under the Open Government Licence – Canada (https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada). title: Segmenting QRIS Readiness Among Traditional Market Traders Using Technology Readiness Index 2.0 and K-Means Clustering
authors: Harvard Kaunang Najoan; Florinda Renda Maria Langitan; Ryalest Maydio Balylo Boka
abstract: Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) is widely available in Indonesian traditional markets, but availability alone does not show whether traders are ready to use it, suggesting that technology readiness may be an important factor beyond physical access to payment infrastructure. This study profiles and segments the technology readiness of 60 smartphone-owning traders at Pasar Beriman Tomohon, North Sulawesi, using the four dimensions of the Technology Readiness Index 2.0 (TRI 2.0): Optimism, Innovativeness, Discomfort, and Insecurity. K-means clustering on standardised dimension scores produced five segments that follow the TRI 2.0 archetypes. The five-cluster solution was chosen on theoretical grounds, because the silhouette check slightly favoured three clusters; the segments are weakly separated and only moderately stable. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha (Innovativeness and Discomfort fell below the 0.60 criterion), and group differences were examined through non-parametric tests. Paranoids formed the largest segment (25.0%) and Pioneers the smallest (11.7%). Insecurity had the higher mean score of the two inhibitor dimensions, exceeding Discomfort. Age showed a stronger demographic association with readiness than merchandise type, and the observed association was concentrated in Innovativeness and Discomfort rather than Insecurity. These findings suggest that segment-differentiated support addressing security and trust concerns may offer a more targeted basis for QRIS adoption programmes among traditional-market traders than uniform market-wide campaigns. Because the sample is small, non-random, and drawn from one market, the results are exploratory.
